sees: frame 1: A light-coloured room background with three icons arranged horizontally: a crowd of small human figures labelled 'CASINOS', a large grey coin with a dollar sign labelled 'CASH', and a chess-knight piece labelled 'CHIPS'. All three elements are static and evenly spaced.

frame 2: The same three icons, but the coin (CASH) has moved right and now sits next to the CHIPS icon. A dashed rectangle outlines both CASH and CHIPS together, grouping them. A curved arrow drawn with a red circle at its tail points from CASINOS up and over to the CHIPS/CASH group, suggesting a directional relationship.

frame 3: The layout is identical to frame 2 — CASINOS on the left, CASH and CHIPS grouped inside a dashed rectangle on the right — with the same curved arrow. The positions appear fully settled; there is no further motion visible.
changed: The CASH coin moved from between CASINOS and CHIPS to beside CHIPS; a dashed grouping box appeared around CASH and CHIPS; a curved arrow appeared pointing from CASINOS to that group.
cause: An animation is illustrating that casinos redirect or convert cash into chips — the arrow and grouping box show that cash and chips belong together as a destination of casino action.
effect: The viewer understands that casinos take cash and exchange it for chips, bundling the two concepts together as the outcome of the casino relationship.
message: Casinos convert your cash into chips, abstracting money into a less emotionally real form.
wouldConfuse: The arrow originates from CASINOS but points toward the CHIPS/CASH group, which could make it ambiguous whether CASINOS is giving chips to players or players are bringing cash to casinos; also, CASH ends up inside the CHIPS group, which may imply they are equivalent rather than sequential.

sees: frame 1: A cartoon man in a dark suit stands facing slightly left in a grey office-like room. He has a neutral/slightly puzzled expression, one arm resting at his side. No text overlay is visible.
frame 2: The same cartoon man in the same pose and room. His expression appears marginally more attentive or engaged, but no meaningful change in posture or scene elements is visible.
frame 3: The same cartoon man, now with a bold orange rectangular label reading 'BIOLOGICAL REALITY' appearing to his right. His expression and pose are unchanged.
changed: A bold orange text label 'BIOLOGICAL REALITY' appeared to the right of the character by frame 3.
cause: The narrator reached a point in the script where this concept is introduced, triggering the text to animate in.
effect: The term 'Biological Reality' is now prominently displayed, signalling that the upcoming or current point is grounded in human biology rather than opinion.
message: The narrator is introducing 'biological reality' as the underlying reason for the behaviour being discussed.
wouldConfuse: The character's expression does not change and he does nothing to indicate the significance of the label; a muted viewer might not understand why this label appeared or what it refers to.

sees: frame 1: A cartoon man in a dark suit stands on the left in a room with a grey radial-burst background. To his right is a large orange rectangle displaying the text 'THE DEFAULT SAFE CHOICE' in white bold letters. The man's eyes are open and he looks neutral.
frame 2: The same scene. The man's eyes are now closed or nearly closed, and his mouth is slightly open — he appears to be speaking or expressing something. The orange sign is unchanged.
frame 3: The same scene again. The man's eyes are open once more and his expression has returned to neutral. The orange sign remains. No other changes.
changed: The character's eyes closed briefly (frame 2) and then reopened (frame 3); his mouth was slightly open in frame 2.
cause: The character is mid-speech — a talking/blinking animation cycle playing while the sign is on screen.
effect: The scene conveys that the presenter is actively talking about 'The Default Safe Choice' while the concept label stays visible.
message: People tend to pick the default, safe option rather than taking a risk.
wouldConfuse: With sound off, the blinking/talking animation is the only cue that the character is speaking; without audio, the scene change feels very minor and the viewer may not register anything is being explained.

sees: frame 1: A cartoon man in a dark suit stands on the left side. The background is split: the left half behind him is white/light grey (like a wall with a window grid), and the right half is a warm yellow-orange. No text overlay.

frame 2: The same character in the same position. To his right, against the yellow-orange background, bold dark text has appeared reading 'HIRE THE CLUMSY ONE' in large stacked lines. The word 'ONE' has an orange highlight behind it.
frame 3: The scene is identical to frame 2 — the character stands on the left, and 'HIRE THE CLUMSY ONE' with the highlighted 'ONE' remains on the right. No further change.
changed: The bold text 'HIRE THE CLUMSY ONE' (with 'ONE' highlighted in orange) appeared on the right side of the screen between frame 1 and frame 2, and remained through frame 3.
cause: The narrator introduced a counter-intuitive recommendation, triggering the key phrase to animate onto the screen.
effect: The provocative phrase 'HIRE THE CLUMSY ONE' is now the focal point, drawing the viewer's attention to an unexpected piece of advice.
message: The narrator is advising that hiring the clumsy (imperfect, relatable) candidate can be advantageous — likely a reference to the pratfall effect.
